highlights.text: one single idea — scattering and dispersing a thing (نَثْرُ الشَّيْءِ وَتَفْرِيقُهُ).
بَذَّرْتُ الْمَالَ أُبَذِّرُهُ تَبْذِيرًا — "I squandered/scattered the wealth,"
a line of poetry naming several watering-places, one of which is "Baddhar"
the bulk/mass of a thing, as distinct from its extremities (shawā).
al-badan — a person's body/torso (plural abdān).
illustrated with a verse about a belted, laboring animal
a single sound root whose core meaning is distinguishing one thing from another
"to separate/divide" a thing (verbal noun faṣl)
the arbiter or judge — the one who decides a matter.
Abū Dhuʾayb, comparing a liquid to "the water of the mountain-clefts."
From a hadith: نَفَقَة فَاصِلَة (a "separating" expenditure)
highlights.note: a hadith, glossed within the hadith

highlights.text: The core idea is putting one thing in the place of another to protect it.
A heap of food (a homonym, unrelated to sense 1).
فَدَيْتُهُ ("I ransomed him") means you shield someone with yourself
"May all peoples be a ransom for you…"
a single core idea: heat and its intensity.
From this sense الْجَحِيم (al-jaḥīm, the blazing fire) takes its name.
He cites al-Aʿshā's line describing a battle-morning in which "death blazes (jāḥim)."
denoting a thing's appearing to a conspicuous, excessive degree
Of SIGHT — being openly/plainly visible.
Of HEARING — uttering aloud (as opposed to keeping secret).
In these the contrast is consistently loud/audible vs. secret/hushed.
a single underlying meaning: al-mayl, "leaning/inclining/deviating."
janaf here names an unjust bias or deviation in how a bequest is made.
a line of poetry in which a she-camel "turns away" (tajānafat) from the bulk of al-Yamāma
gathering/coalescing together, and to its hardening or becoming compact.
the human body: given as the primary instance of that notion of a mass gathered and firm.
Citation: the poet al-Ṭirimmāḥ — "of it [there is] congealed [blood] and fresh gore"
as a sound root carrying two distinct meanings, plus one usage that fits neither.
Cited in a supplication: "Do not make the Qur'an a māḥil against us" — i.e., do not let the Qur'an testify against us [before God] for having abandoned following it
highlights.note: a supplication, glossed by Ibn Fāris

highlights.text: a single sound root whose core idea is a colour.
النَّعْجَة (naʿja), the ewe of the domestic flock
as though the people had been fed mutton at supper, "so they are naʿijūn, their necks already drooping."
one basic idea: to butt (nataha)
Core meaning: butting/goring. Said of a ram: yantihu, "it butts."
Proverbial idiom: "the night is dark and the rams are butting each other"
a single sound root whose core idea is the opening-up or splitting-open of something.
a watercourse "cleaves" the earth
a verse by Abū Dhuʾayb describing a tent pitched by reeds and a sweet, water-rich stream
the opposite of ṭahāra (purity/cleanness) — i.e. impurity, filth.
something najis or najas [two forms of the same adjective] is qadhir — filthy, dirty.
he cites the poet Sāʿida al-Hudhalī, who calls grey hair/old age an "incurable disease"
one root with a single core meaning: drinking milk from an udder or a breast.
رَضِعَ / يَرْضَعُ — "(an infant) suckled / suckles."
مُرْضِعَةٌ describes her in the very act of nursing
a stingy man so mean that he suckles his own she-camels himself
a single core meaning: tenderness, affectionate inclination, and compassion.
رَحِمَهُ يَرْحَمُهُ means to have mercy on someone
a line of the poet Zuhayr in which "God and al-ruḥum" protect a pious man from stumbling
al-rumḥ (الرمح) = "the spear/lance" — the ordinary, well-known weapon.
a line of poetry describing a time when the poet's she-camels — young and old alike — had not yet had "weapons" (silāḥ) turned against them by the pasture
One core meaning: good fortune/condition, and what a person acquires of good.
al-rīsh — good; al-riyāsh — wealth
illustrated with a line of poetry contrasting a patron who "rishes" (builds up) a client with one who wears him down (barā)
Ibn Fāris discusses the hadith term al-rāʾish ("the intermediary," in "the bribe-giver, bribe-taker, and intermediary")
derives the root س-ه-م (s-h-m) from two distinct origins.
To "asham" (asḥama) means to draw lots with someone, so each party wins whatever falls to him.
"he cast lots (sāhama), and was among those who lost the draw (al-mudḥaḍīn)."
a single, consistent root meaning to lower oneself down (taṭāmun)
سَجَدَ (sajada) is to lower or humble oneself.
Ḥumayd's line comparing camels bowing under slack reins to "the prostration of the Christians to their lords,"
a single core idea: exceeding the limit
فِي الْأَمْرِ سَرَفٌ = "there is excess in the matter," i.e. going past the proper amount.
Ṭarafa's line about "a man ignorant of heart (sarif al-fuʾād)" who mistakes insults for sweetness
a ḥadīth that the third washing in ablution is "honor" (sharaf) but the fourth is "excess"
one core idea: something continuing on while also passing away/flowing off
"sayyabtu d-dābbata" — to turn an animal loose, letting it go wherever it wants, unrestrained.
two distinct root meanings (aṣlān mutabāyinān)
al-thullah is a group of people,
Labīd tells of an onslaught that "brought them to al-thalal".
Zuhayr addresses two people who came to the rescue of the confederates (al-aḥlāf)
One core meaning: the gathering of one thing to another
al-khaṣf — patching a sandal
al-ikhtiṣāf — a naked person covering himself with broad leaves, taken over his private parts.
illustrated with a line of poetry by a Hudhalī poet comparing an eagle's nose-tip
highlights.note: a Hudhalī poet, lived into Islam

highlights.text: a single core sense: permanence and constant attachment
خَلَدَ (and أَخْلَدَ) = he stayed, remained, endured.
أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ = he stuck fast / cleaved to the ground.
a line of Ibn Aḥmar contrasting the beloved's endurance
two distinct underlying senses
From this sound-sense comes زُمْرَة (zumrah), "a group/company"
A ḥadīth forbids "the earnings of al-zammārah." Transmitters gloss zammārah as al-zāniyah (the adulteress/fornicatress).
highlights.note: a hadith and its transmitters' gloss
